To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1 the incidence of PTSD after trauma exposure in children and adolescents was 15.95% (95% confidence interval [CI] 11.5-21.5), and 2 the incidence varied according to the trauma type and the sex of the child, with the highest rates found in girls exposed to interpersonal traumas.

the rate of PTSD in children and adolescents exposed to traumatic events is high (approximately 16%); that the rate is higher in girls (approximately 32%) than in boys (approximately 9%) and in those exposed to interpersonal traumas (approximately 32%), compared to those exposed to non interpersonal traumas (9%); and that the rate is similar when assessed by different interview methods and informants (parent, teacher, child).

The overall rate of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTST) in children and adolescents was 15.5% (95% confidence interval [CI] 11.4-20.7) and the rate of post-trauma psychiatric disorder (PTSD and/or depression and/or anxiety) was 25.2% (95%CI 19.3-32.3).

the development of PTSD and the role of trauma and other risk and protective factors in its development.
the development, assessment and treatment of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTS) in children and young people.
